src: A 77-year-old man was admitted with exertional dyspnea and bilateral pitting edema of both legs.
Her past medical history included hypertension and type 2 diabetes mellitus for ten years.
Vital signs on admission: heart rate 112 bpm, respiratory rate 24 breaths/min, blood pressure 90/60 mmHg, temperature 38.5 °C and SpO2 91% on room air.
He has a long history of chronic kidney disease and chronic obstructive pulmonary disease.
must: bệnh phổi tắc nghẽn mạn tính

src: Laboratory tests showed anemia with a hemoglobin of 8.2 g/dL, hyponatremia and a serum creatinine of 2.1 mg/dL.
The patient reported a low-grade fever, night sweats and unintentional weight loss over three months.
The patient received metformin 500 mg orally twice daily, and furosemide 40 mg was given intravenously.
No adverse drug reactions were recorded, but dose adjustment was required when the eGFR fell below 30 mL/min/1.73 m2.
Polypharmacy, frailty and falls were common among older adults admitted to the geriatric ward.
She was discharged from hospital on day 7, and no readmission was recorded within 30 days.
Anticoagulant therapy was started for atrial fibrillation, and a proton pump inhibitor was prescribed to prevent gastrointestinal bleeding.
On examination, she had jaundice, ascites and splenomegaly, with no peripheral lymphadenopathy.
Comorbidities included dyslipidemia, gout and osteoarthritis, and hypokalemia was corrected with oral potassium chloride.
The patient presented with melena and hematemesis, and upper gastrointestinal bleeding was suspected.
The anaemia was chronic, whereas the myocardial ischaemia on the ECG was new.
must_any: thiếu máu cục bộ cơ tim

src: The complete blood count was normal, serology confirmed viral hepatitis, and his brother had end-stage renal disease.
